q: 1. Reinforced cement concrete is equally strong in taking
explain: By combining concrete (strong in compression) with steel reinforcement (strong in tension) and proper detailing for shear, RCC is designed to resist tensile, compressive, and shear stresses effectively.

q: 2. The commonly used material in the manufacture of cement is
explain: Limestone (calcareous material, source of lime/CaO) is the principal raw material used along with clay in cement manufacture.

q: 3. The mixture of different ingredients of cement, is burnt at
explain: The raw mixture of cement ingredients is burnt at approximately 1400°C, the clinkering temperature, to form cement clinker.

q: 4. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following:
options: Tricalcium silicate (C3S) generates more heat of hydration
Tricalcium silicate (C3S) has more resistance to sulphate attack
explain: C3S actually has less resistance to sulphate/chemical attack (compared to C2S), so the statement claiming it has more resistance is incorrect.

q: 5. The high strength of rapid hardening cement at early stage, is due to
explain: Rapid hardening cement contains a higher lime content and increased C3S proportion, which along with finer grinding results in higher early strength.

q: 6. The commercial name of white and coloured cement in India is
explain: Colocrete, rainbow cement, and silvicrete/snowcem are all commercial trade names used in India for white and coloured cements.

q: 7. The apparent specific gravity of an aggregate is defined as
options: the weight of oven dry aggregate divided by its absolute volume, excluding the natural pores in the aggregate particles
the weight of oven dry aggregate divided by its absolute volume, excluding the natural process in the aggregate particles
the weight of aggregate required to fill a container of unit volume
the difference in weight of the aggregate in saturated surface dry condition and in moist condition
explain: Apparent specific gravity is the weight of oven-dry aggregate divided by its absolute (solid) volume, excluding the natural pores within the particles.

q: 8. Bulking of sand is
options: mixing of different sizes of sand particles
explain: Bulking of sand refers to the increase in volume of sand due to the film of moisture surrounding the sand particles, which causes swelling when wetted.

q: 9. The minimum particle size of coarse aggregate is
explain: Coarse aggregate begins where fine aggregate ends — particles retained on the 4.75 mm sieve are classified as coarse aggregate, so its minimum size is 4.75 mm.

q: 10. Fineness modulus of fine aggregate is between
explain: The fineness modulus of fine aggregate (sand) typically ranges between 2.0 and 3.5, indicating its overall particle size distribution.

q: 11. The ratio of the volume of moist sand to the volume of dry sand is known as
explain: The bulking factor is the ratio of the volume of moist (bulked) sand to the volume of the same sand in dry condition, reflecting the increase in volume due to moisture films between particles.

q: 12. The function of fine aggregate is:
options: to assist in producing workability and uniformity in the mixture
to assist the cement paste to hold the coarse aggregate particles in suspension
to promote plasticity in the mixture and prevent possible segregation of paste and coarse aggregate
explain: Fine aggregate serves multiple purposes in concrete — improving workability, uniformity, holding coarse particles in suspension, and preventing segregation — so all listed functions are correct.

q: 13. An aggregate having all the pores filled with water but having dry surface is called
explain: Saturated Surface Dry (SSD) condition is defined as the state where all internal pores are filled with water but the surface itself is free of surface moisture.

q: 14. The resistance of an aggregate to compressive force is known as
explain: The aggregate crushing value test measures the resistance of aggregate to gradually applied compressive (crushing) load.

q: 15. The resistance of an aggregate to wear is known as
explain: The abrasion value test (e.g., Los Angeles test) measures an aggregate's resistance to wear caused by rubbing/attrition.

q: 16. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: the maximum size of a coarse aggregate, is 75mm and minimum 4.75mm
the maximum size of a fine aggregate, is 4.75mm and minimum 0.075mm
the material having particles of size varying from 0.06mm to 0.002mm is known as slit
the material having particles of size less than 0.002mm, is known as clay
explain: All the given size classifications for coarse aggregate, fine aggregate, silt, and clay are correct according to standard particle size definitions.

q: 17. The light weight aggregates may be obtained from
explain: Lightweight aggregates such as pumice and scoria are derived from volcanic sources, which contain porous, low-density material.

q: 18. The aggregate containing moisture in pores and having its surface dry, is known as
explain: Saturated surface dry (SSD) aggregate is defined as aggregate whose pores are filled with moisture but whose surface is dry, neither absorbing nor contributing extra water to the mix.

q: 19. Log Angles machine is used to test the aggregate for
explain: The Los Angeles Abrasion testing machine is specifically used to determine the abrasion resistance (hardness) of aggregates.

q: 20. If 20 kg of a coarse aggregate is sieved through 80mm, 40 mm, 20 mm, 10 mm, 4.75 mm, 2.36 mm, 1.18 mm, 600 micron, 300 micron and 150 micron standard sieves and the weights retained are 0 kg, 2 kg, 5 kg, 6 kg, 4 kg, 3kg respectively, the fineness modulus of the aggregate, is
explain: Fineness modulus = sum of cumulative percentage retained on standard sieves ÷ 100. Calculating cumulative % retained (0,10,35,65,85,100 for 6 sieves shown, remaining sieves 100 each for 4 finer sieves) gives a total of 740/100 = 7.40.

q: 21. Ware house pack of cement means
options: pressure exertion of the bags of upper layers
pressure compaction of bag on lower layer
explain: Warehouse pack refers to the compaction/hardening effect on lower cement bags caused by the pressure of bags stacked above them during storage.

q: 22. The most useless aggregate is one whose surface texture is
explain: A glossy surface texture prevents proper bonding with cement paste, making such aggregate the least useful/desirable for concrete construction.

q: 23. If the engineer-in-charge approves, the 10cm cubes may be used for the work test of concrete provided maximum nominal size of aggregate, does not exceed
explain: Smaller 10cm cubes can be substituted for standard 15cm cubes only when the maximum nominal aggregate size does not exceed 20mm, to maintain a valid size ratio between specimen and aggregate.

q: 24. An ordinary Portland cement when tested for its fineness, should not leave any residue on I.S. sieve no. 9, more than
explain: As per IS specifications, the residue retained on the 90-micron (IS sieve no. 9) sieve when testing OPC fineness should not exceed 10%.

q: 25. The specific surface of cement is expressed in
explain: Specific surface (fineness) of cement is a measure of surface area per unit mass of the cement particles, and is therefore expressed in units of mm² per gram (mm²/g), or more commonly cm²/g.

q: 26. The concrete mix which causes difficulty in obtaining a smooth finish, is known to possess
explain: High internal friction between aggregate particles (harsh mix) resists smooth movement of material against the formwork/trowel, making it difficult to achieve a smooth surface finish.

q: 27. For reinforced cement concrete lintels and slabs, the nominal size of coarse aggregate should not exceed.
explain: For thin RCC members such as lintels and slabs, the maximum nominal coarse aggregate size is generally restricted to 20 mm to ensure proper placement around reinforcement.

q: 28. The cement whose strength is a little lower than the ordinary cement during the first three months but attains afterwards the same strength, is known as
explain: Low-heat Portland cement gains strength more slowly in the early months due to reduced C3S/C3A content, but eventually catches up to match the strength of ordinary cement.

q: 29. The sum of percentage of tricalcium silicate and dicalcium silicate for portlad cement varies from
explain: In ordinary Portland cement, the combined percentage of C3S and C2S (the main strength-giving silicate compounds) typically ranges from about 70% to 80%.

q: 30. For construction of structures in seawater, the cement generally preferred to, is
explain: Portland-pozzolana cement offers better resistance to sulphate and chloride attack from seawater, making it the preferred choice for marine structures.

q: 31. The size of fine aggregated does not exceed
explain: By standard classification, fine aggregate particles must pass through the 4.75mm IS sieve, so their size does not exceed 4.75mm.

q: 32. Shrinkage in cement concrete can be reduced by using
explain: All these measures - low w/c ratio, reduced cement content, properly proportioned mix, and use of pre-saturated aggregates - help in minimizing drying shrinkage of concrete.

q: 33. The specification of a cement bag for storage, are
explain: A standard cement bag has all these specifications together - 50 kg weight, about 18 cm height, roughly 3000 sq.cm plan area, and about 35 litres volume.

q: 34. Light weight concrete is used for
explain: Due to its lower density and reduced structural strength, light weight concrete is mainly suitable for non-load bearing walls and partitions.

q: 35. The bulking of aggregate is due to
explain: Bulking of fine aggregate (sand) occurs specifically due to the presence of moisture content, which creates surface tension films that push particles apart.

q: 36. The maximum bulking of sand occurs at a moisture content of
explain: Maximum bulking of sand typically occurs at a relatively low moisture content of around 5% to 8% by volume, before further water addition reduces bulking (as per the given key, 5%).

q: 37. An aggregate which passes through 25mm I.S. sieve and is retained on 20mm sieve, is said to be flaky if its least dimension is less than
explain: The mean dimension is (25+20)/2 = 22.5mm; applying the flakiness criterion (least dimension < 3/5 mean) gives 0.6 × 22.5 = 13.5mm.

q: 38. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: 5% of the total aggregates for low workability with a coarse grading
10% of the total aggregates for low workability with a coarse grading
20% of the total aggregates for a mix having high workability with fine grading
explain: These percentages represent standard recommended proportions of fines depending on the required workability and grading type, so all the given statements are correct together.

q: 39. For a good concrete
options: aggregates should be hard and durable
cement should be sufficient to produce the required strength
water should be free form organic material
mixing of ingredients should be done thoroughly so as to produce homogeneity
explain: Good quality concrete requires all these conditions to be satisfied together - hard/durable aggregates, adequate cement, clean water, and thorough homogeneous mixing.

q: 40. The importance of storing the various ingredients of concrete is
options: to maintain the uniformity of grading
to maintain the uniformity of moisture
to maintain the strength of materials
explain: Proper storage of concrete ingredients helps maintain consistent grading and moisture content of materials, which directly affects mix uniformity — both a and b matter.

q: 41. The capacity of ware house depends upon
options: floor area occupied by one cement bag
height to which the bags are piled
explain: Warehouse storage capacity is determined by both the floor area per bag and the permissible pile height together, so both factors apply.

q: 42. For the construction of cement concrete dams, the maximum permissible size of the aggregates is
explain: For mass concrete dam construction, larger aggregate sizes are permitted to reduce cement content and heat of hydration; the maximum permissible size specified in this text is 60 mm.

q: 43. Find the gel space ratio of concrete with following data: cement = 50 kg, Weight of water = 20 kg
explain: Substituting the given cement and water quantities into the standard gel-space ratio formula (relating the volume of hydration products to total space occupied) gives a ratio of approximately 0.91.

q: 44. The maximum percentage of chemical ingredient of cement is that of
explain: Lime (calcium oxide, CaO) is present in the highest proportion among the chemical constituents of Portland cement, typically around 60-65%.
